title: Reel 2 opening; gigging with Joe Steele in Boston
summary: After a reel change, Schaap recaps Boston. Waters says the Steele gigs were mostly dancing, that he had no free-solo band, and that money came from commercial jobs.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Testing, testing, sounds pretty good. We've now moved to reel 2 of those being done here on this Sunday the 6th of June, 1982, just about 5 minutes past 4 o'clock as we begin the second reel. And we're going to pick up the story in Boston at the turn of the '20's. Let's do a little checking off here. Shortly after your 18th birthday or in 1920, you're still in short pants, you can go to Boston. You go to school there, you supported yourself primarily the first year through a hard-working -

but gradually you were able to build up a musical career there, which led you to, among other things, associates of your brother Herman in his little musical semi-pro kind of Elks' activities and what have you. And eventually you were able to get something that we would consider a jazz name gig and, when you met a pianist by the name of Joe Steele, who was a graduate already of the Conservatory -
And this you would date around '21 or '22.
Yeah, in that period, see, yeah.
Right. Joe Steele had a regular working band or you were just giggin' -
No, giggin', yeah. Giggin'. But I did quite a lot with Joe, see, particularly weekends, you know, see.
But you were able to get your solos in, was it as much fun -

No - no, no. I didn't have no fun with the solos until I was in - who did I work with now, what band did I work with when I had a lot of, to tell you the truth I don't remember working with any band that really I was real free. Because, I mean, I liked a little money too, you know, see. So to make money I had to work with people who payed the most money, see. And the people who paid the most money even then and as of now, it's commercial jobs, you see what I'm talking about?
And commercial jobs to you is -
Dancing, and the band quits and things like that, you know.
